$comment: Coverage gate config for @namzu/sdk. Consumed by .github/scripts/check-sdk-module-coverage.mjs and check-sdk-test-presence.mjs. The bucket rules were ratified in ses_006-test-coverage-sprint.
$comment_pricing: `pricing` is `required` with a measured floor, and the floor only means anything because its generated rate table is excluded from coverage in vitest.config.ts. Measured with the table IN: 299 lines, 282 of them the generated data, all counted covered the moment anything imports the module — so the aggregate read 100% while describing almost nothing, and the resolver could have lost a third of its lines and still cleared 97%. Measured with it OUT: 17 lines and 10 branches, all in index.ts, 100%/100%. Floor is measured minus 3 per the policy in check-sdk-module-coverage.mjs. Note the module is small enough that 3 points is less than one branch, so any uncovered branch in the resolver fails this gate — that is intended, not an accident of rounding.
$comment_coverageFloors: `runtime`, `store` and `manager` were the three critical modules with no floor; they are added here by issue #502. They were already `required`, so this is not a claim that they are untested -- `runtime` alone carries 192 test files, 187 of them under `runtime/query` -- it is the measurement that was missing, because test presence is not coverage -- a module can carry two hundred passing tests and still have whole failure paths that nothing executes. They were set from a measurement taken on the parent commit (718 files and 7355 tests, unchanged on the commit that landed them, 720 files and 7381 tests), which under the counter then in use read `runtime` 91.18% lines / 89.69% branches, `store` 93.23% / 88.33%, `manager` 81.63% / 88.91%. Those three figures are kept as history, and are labelled as history: vitest 4 replaced the counter, no floor in this file is derived from them any more, and the current measurements -- and the current floors, every one of them -- are in `$comment_vitest4_remeasurement`. `manager`'s floor is still the lowest line floor of the eleven, because `manager` also holds the lowest measured line coverage of the eleven; the next phase raises it by landing tests on the coordinators under `src/manager/` against their own failure paths -- `session/`, `resident/`, `project/`, and delegated agents under `manager/agent/`, where `lifecycle.ts` is what holds their budget -- rather than by raising the number. Two things to know before trusting any of these figures. One is that slack is now uniform: every floor here is `measured - 3` by construction, so there is no spread of slack to reason about. The v3-era enumeration that used to sit in this paragraph -- 2.76 points at `directory`, through 3.00 at `pricing`, to 47.48 at `connector` -- is deliberately not restated, because it described a calibration that no longer exists, and a paragraph asserting slack figures that do not match the floors beneath it is the defect this paragraph was corrected for. The other is that the branch denominator is the less stable of the two measures, and it is what the 3 points are for. Under vitest 3, five coverage runs over the same `store` sources gave four different branch denominators (3289, 3290, 3291, 3292) and an aggregate ranging 88.32% to 88.36%. Under vitest 4, two runs agreed exactly, to four decimals, on 21387 branches and 83.62%. Two identical runs are better than five disagreeing ones, but they are a sample of two and not a distribution, so treat the slack as headroom for edits rather than as a guarantee about the measurement, and do not read a delta smaller than a tenth of a point as a signal. And a branch floor cannot see a module LOSE a path: deleting untested code takes its branch records with it and the ratio can go UP, so the line floor is set alongside the branch floor and not instead of it.
$comment_vitest4_remeasurement: RE-DERIVED 2026-09-18 from the vitest 4 measurement. Every floor above is floor(measured_v4 - 3): the policy this file has always stated, applied to a new instrument. No threshold was relaxed to make a run pass, and that is the sentence a reader six months from now needs in order to tell this apart from a quiet loosening -- the policy is unchanged, the calibration is new, and no floor moved because coverage was lost. It cannot have been lost: the two measurements differ ONLY in the vitest version. Same worktree, same config, same source tree, and the same 744 files and 7541 tests, all passing, in both runs. Vitest 4 replaced the v8 provider's remapping (`v8-to-istanbul` becomes `ast-v8-to-istanbul`), so the old numbers were never comparable to the new ones. The decisive evidence is one file, `src/utils/hash.ts`. Vitest 3 counted 20 lines in it and called 9 covered, 45%. Vitest 4 counts 7 and calls 1 covered. The file has 32 physical lines, 20 of them non-blank, and exactly 7 executable statements: 2 in `hashToolResult`, 4 in `buildToolResultHashes`, 1 in `stableDigest`. v4 is right. v3 was counting non-executable source lines as coverage units, and v4's lcov says so line by line -- `DA:28,2950`, `stableDigest`'s single line, executed 2950 times, against `DA:4,0`, `DA:5,0`, `DA:11,0`, `DA:12,0`, `DA:13,0`, `DA:15,0`, every line of the two functions that no test calls. The 13 extra lines v3 counted are filler that any executed file scores as covered the moment it loads, which is why the old percentages were INFLATED rather than merely different, and why the drop is a correction. The same effect package-wide, over an identical 548-file set: lines 66584 -> 26798, branches 23649 -> 21387, functions 3975 -> 5563, statements 66584 -> 30012, and as percentages lines 90.62 -> 89.43, branches 89.09 -> 83.62. Old floor -> new floor, with the v4 measurement each new floor comes from: advisory 94/91 -> 95/90 (98.3871/93.6416), bridge 96/95 -> 95/88 (98.8889/91.6049), bus 94/91 -> 93/87 (96.3115/90.8257), connector 47/84 -> 90/81 (93.7035/84.8321), directory 85/82 -> 86/80 (89.6996/83.8542), manager 78/85 -> 73/79 (76.2590/82.8094), pricing 97/97 -> 97/97 (100.0000/100.0000), rag 92/92 -> 92/89 (95.5923/92.6407), registry 93/90 -> 93/87 (96.5471/90.1454), runtime 88/86 -> 89/82 (92.5215/85.9372), store 90/85 -> 88/78 (91.9895/81.7416). THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE TRUSTING THESE. (1) The re-derivation TIGHTENS four line floors, because some v3 floors had been set below measured - 3: advisory 94 -> 95, directory 85 -> 86, runtime 88 -> 89, and connector 47 -> 90 by a wide margin. connector was checked rather than assumed, and the finding is that the old 47 has no reason recorded anywhere in this file. It sat 47.48 points below what connector measured, which is not a ratchet: connector would have had to lose more than half its coverage before the gate noticed. The paragraph that used to sit in `$comment_coverageFloors` described the anomaly -- the lowest floor here, and the loosest by an order of magnitude -- without ever saying why it was set there while every other row followed the file's own measured - 3 policy, and no other passage in this file mentions it. With no recorded reason, this row is derived like every other row and there is no exception to carry; the uniform policy is the whole of the decision, and it is recorded that way on purpose rather than left as a hedge. If a reason does exist outside this file -- in the owner's memory, in issue #502, or in a commit message -- restoring connector as a deliberate exception costs one number and one sentence here. The cost of NOT restoring it is the half worth naming: connector now fails the gate on a 3.7-point loss instead of a 47.5-point one, so a coverage loss there is caught now rather than never, which is what a floor is for and why this row is not being left loose on a guess. (2) The apparent outlier did not survive checking. `manager` falls 5.80 points on the count-weighted aggregate this gate computes, four times any other module, which reads exactly like a module losing coverage. It is re-weighting, not loss: the same module's UNWEIGHTED mean of per-file line percentages falls only 1.79, and on that measure all eleven modules sit within 1.8 points of where they were, spread -1.79 to +0.18. v4 counts about 0.42 lines per line v3 counted and does so unevenly per file, so an aggregate that weights files by line count moves without any file's own percentage moving -- `src/manager/resident/learning.ts` goes 386 counted lines to 131 and stays at 100%, `src/manager/resident/store.ts` goes 203 to 61 and goes UP, 92.61 to 93.44. (3) Branch deltas do NOT decompose as cleanly as line deltas: unweighted they spread -7.49 to 0.00, because branch points are the unit the two remappers disagree about most -- v3 synthesised them from transpiled JavaScript, v4 derives them from the AST -- so these branch floors are a weaker ratchet in relative terms than the line floors, and should be watched rather than trusted to exactly 3 points. `$comment_coverageFloors` no longer restates the v3 slack enumeration, for the same reason it is gone from there.
$comment_train_remeasurement: RE-DERIVED 2026-09-22 at the tip of the session/turn train (remove-run), as spec item 2.6 requires: every floor is again floor(measured - 3), measured by `pnpm --filter @namzu/sdk test:coverage` over 760 files and 7740 tests, all passing. Changed rows, old -> new (measured lines/branches): bridge 95/88 -> 95/89 (98.9305/92.1700), manager 73/79 -> 75/79 (78.2701/82.7502), runtime 89/82 -> 88/82 (91.8630/85.1077), store 88/78 -> 90/79 (93.1207/82.6313). Every other row already equalled floor(measured - 3) and is unchanged: advisory 98.3871/93.6416, bus 96.3115/90.8257, connector 93.7035/84.8321, directory 89.6996/83.8542, pricing 100/100, rag 95.5923/92.6407, registry 96.5517/90.2087. runtime is the one floor that goes DOWN, by one line point: the train replaced `store/run` and the run-era runtime paths with the session log, turn recorder and fork code, and its line measurement moved 92.5215 -> 91.8630 across that rewrite. That is the policy applied to a changed module, not a relaxation to make a run pass; the branch floor is unchanged, and the figures in `$comment_vitest4_remeasurement` remain as the history they are.
$comment_baseline_exempt: `baselineExempt` means ZERO-TESTED, per check-sdk-test-presence.mjs's own docblock. It had drifted badly: seven of its nine entries carried tests -- `utils` had 25 files -- so the list said 'these have no tests' about modules that did. A routing document that is false is worse than none, because the next person picks the wrong module to work on. Audited and corrected in ses_020, which left the two that genuinely had none. Both graduated to `required` in issue #502, in the commit that added their tests, so the list is empty and stays here as the bucket a new module lands in while it is dark -- empty is the state this file is supposed to be in, not one to refill. Measured on the commit BEFORE those tests landed: `model-router` 100% lines and branches, all 14 and all 8 of them, because `compaction.ts` calls `resolveTaskModel` on every compaction and `compaction-model-routing.test.ts` asserts every step of the chain from there -- covered, and covered from another module's tests, which is the gap the bucket was naming: nothing failed if the resolver was wrong for a task type compaction never asks about. `persona` measured 52.99% lines / 81.48% branches / 40% functions (62/117, 22/27, 2/5), every uncovered line in `persona/assembler.ts`, and every one of them a field a host sets: expertise domains, constraints, tool guidance, output discipline, and the whole of `mergePersonas` and `withSessionContext`. After their tests `persona` reads 117/117 lines, 58/58 branches, 5/5 functions. Neither carries a `coverageFloors` entry yet -- a floor for them is a separate ratchet, and these numbers are recorded here so it has something measured to ratchet from. Moving a module here into `required` asserts only that it HAS a test, which is what this gate checks -- coverage is the separate, opt-in `coverageFloors` claim.
